analyzed_vuln.description: Use-after-poison occurs because dead-code simplification removes/replaces assignment expressions without keeping ProgramUsage and variable-declaration state consistent, then later dead-assignment analysis calls ProgramUsage::get -> Variable::initialValue() on a Variable whose declaration-owned initial-value expression pointer (fDeclaration->value()) is no longer valid in the arena pool. The crash manifests at Variable::initialValue in skia/src/sksl/ir/SkSLVariable.cpp:15, but the root cause is unsafe mutation during optimization in Compiler::simplifyExpression (dead_assignment/delete_left path).
analyzed_vuln.conditions: In the skruntimeeffect harness, attacker-controlled SkSL source is compiled with optimization/dead-code elimination enabled. A crafted shader (like the PoC with struct/global/local assignments and malformed trailing bytes) drives simplifyExpression through dead_assignment/self-assignment folding during CFG scan. This mutates expressions and usage counts; subsequent ProgramUsage::isDead/get queries a variable initial value via fDeclaration->value().get() after the underlying pooled expression has been invalidated/poisoned, producing the ASan use-after-poison read.
